dialect: Classical Latin (Ciceronian and Caesarian prose norms), macrons marked on terms

profile.grammar_notes: Copula sum/esse for identity and location; est/sunt also states existence ('there is'). No articles. Six cases carry roles (nominative subject, accusative object, genitive of, dative to/for, ablative by/with/in); word order is free, so endings, not position, show who does what. Verb endings mark person, so subject pronouns are usually dropped. Negation with non; questions with -ne, nonne, num, and interrogatives quis/quid. Coordination et, -que, sed; relative qui, quae, quod. Closed sets: personal pronouns (ego, tū, nōs, vōs), sum paradigm, prepositions with accusative vs ablative, the relative pronoun, demonstratives hic/ille/is. Modal jobs: possum (can), volō (want), dēbeō (must), eō (go), veniō (come), habeō (have). Reading slice: nothing phrased as conversation.
